newsitem.title: USA: EndoVascular Tech trials fully enrolled.
newsitem.headline: EndoVascular Tech trials fully enrolled.

text.p: EndoVascular Technologies Inc on Monday said the Phase II clinical trial of its Tube EGS system for use in surgically repairing an abdominal aortic aneurysm is now fully enrolled.
With 88 people in the EGS group and 90 in a control group, the trial is designed to compare mortality, complications and length of hospital stay of the patients.

Preliminary results of the trial show that in the EGS patient group, the Tube EndoGraft prosthesis was successfully delivered and implanted in 83 of 88 attempted procedures, representing 94% technical success.
Endovascular Technologies reported no 30-day mortality in the EGS group compared to a 3.3 percent mortality rate in the surgical control group.
Also, the company reported no serious complications, which it defined as the occurrence of myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure requiring dialysis, or bowel ischemia.

In the control group, three surgical patients experienced myocardial infarction, but no other serious complications reported. The mean hospital stay for patients in the EGS group was 2.4 days compared to 8.2 days for patients who underwent standard surgery.
